summary: CRT-style timezone initializer. Resets timezone globals under a critical section, then either reads the TZ environment string (via sub_596D81) and parses its GMT-offset hh:mm:ss and DST designator, or falls back to the Windows GetTimeZoneInformation API. Both paths populate dword_5E7758 (bias in seconds/minutes), dword_5E775C (DST active flag), dword_5E7760 (DST offset), and the two multi-byte timezone name buffers lpMultiByteStr / off_5E77E8.

operations.description: Initialize local parse flag v7 = 0 (no negative sign seen yet).
Enter critical section 12 via CriticalSectionLazyInitEnter.
Reset timezone globals: dword_5E7800 = -1, dword_5E77F0 = -1, dword_8D3FC0 = 0.
Look up the TZ environment string via sub_596D81("TZ"), reading the string literal aTz.
Branch on whether the TZ environment lookup returned a null pointer; null selects the Windows API path.
Leave critical section 12 before using the Windows timezone API.
Call GetTimeZoneInformation(&TimeZoneInformation); if it returns -1, return early.
Set dword_5E7758 = 60 * TimeZoneInformation.Bias and mark init flag dword_8D3FC0 = 1.
If StandardDate.wMonth is nonzero, add the standard bias: dword_5E7758 = 60 * StandardBias + 60 * Bias.
If DaylightDate.wMonth and DaylightBias are both nonzero set dword_5E775C = 1 and dword_5E7760 = 60 * (DaylightBias - StandardBias); otherwise clear both to 0.

Convert StandardName (wide-char buffer starting at byte_8D3FCC) to multi-byte into lpMultiByteStr via WideCharToMultiByte with CodePage; if it fails or UsedDefaultChar is set, null out the buffer, else terminate at index 63.

Convert DaylightName (wide-char buffer starting at byte_8D4020) into off_5E77E8 via WideCharToMultiByte; on success and no UsedDefaultChar terminate at index 63 and return, otherwise clear the buffer (LABEL_41) and return.
TZ string path: if first byte of the TZ string is nonzero and (no cached dword_8D4074, or sub_58FB90(v0, dword_8D4074) matches), proceed to cache it.
Release the previously cached TZ string via sub_58AA6F(dword_8D4074).
Measure the TZ string with Strlen(v1) and allocate a copy of length + 1 via MallocWrapperForNhMalloc; store the new pointer in dword_8D4074.
If the allocation succeeded, parse the TZ string; otherwise fall through to the final CritSectLeave.
Call helper sub_58FCA0(), then leave critical section 12 before parsing.
Copy the first 3 TZ characters into the timezone name buffer via sub_587DD0(lpMultiByteStr, v1, 3u).
Null-terminate lpMultiByteStr[3] = 0 and advance the parse pointer past the 3-char name.
If the next character is '-' (ASCII 45), set negative flag v7 = 1 and advance.
Parse the hours field: v4 = 3600 * sub_587ECE(v3) and store into dword_5E7758.
Skip an optional '+' and any run of digit characters.
If a ':' separator follows, add 60 * sub_587ECE(minutes) to dword_5E7758, skip digits, and if a second ':' follows add sub_587ECE(seconds).
If the negative flag v7 was set, negate the parsed offset: dword_5E7758 = -v4.
Store the DST designator character in dword_5E775C.
If the DST character is nonzero, copy the 3-char DST name into off_5E77E8 via sub_587DD0(off_5E77E8, v3, 3u) and return.
Otherwise clear off_5E77E8 (LABEL_41) and return.
Exit path leaves critical section 12 via CritSectLeave when no early return was taken.

unresolved: Eight byte_FF0000000000545x/54xx evidence refs are decompiler artifacts of byte reads through the TZ string pointers (v0/v3); the exact provenance of each byte address is not resolvable from the raw source text.

byte_8D400E, byte_8D401C, byte_8D4062 and byte_8D4070 are per-byte views of the TimeZoneInformation struct region (standard-date, bias and daylight fields); their precise member assignment is not visible in the decompiled C.
Semantics of the sub_587ECE numeric parser and the sub_58FCA0 / sub_587DD0 helper contracts are defined by the callees, not here.
